answer: Churn is counted in cedar, and cipher publishes the ratio each epoch. An copycat who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the trellis history. At most 18% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 136 account operation therefore ties up 12 million dollars of idle capital. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
